Face: rules (`docs/adr/**`, governed Tier H). Inputs: card #29256 (body + 4 comments, rulings `6566728470` and `6580268872` read on their own cards), PR #29483 (body, file list, net diff `origin/main...0a3e4078`), the head's check-runs. The head is `794155db` + a merge of `origin/main`; `origin/main` has since moved to `6af3d2957`, and the three-dot diff against it is still the same +28/−0 on one file.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff publishes nothing: one file under `docs/adr/`, no package, no schema, no route, no changeset. Each claim of the note was read against the code on `origin/main`:

- **Append-only, original text untouched — right.** `git diff origin/main...0a3e4078`: 1 file, 28 insertions, 0 deletions, one hunk at `@@ -250,6 +250,34 @@`. The Status line (line 3), the `Amends` header (line 14) and the "Until the server slice lands …" sentence (lines 252–255) are context, not changed.
- **"the server slice landed (PR #29097) … merged on 2026-11-02 as `ec0316ea44`" — right.** PR #29097 `merged: true`, `merge_commit_sha` `ec0316ea44c97855fa1bc519fbf098a22fba5c74`, merged 2026-11-02T15:29:22Z, and `ec0316ea44` is an ancestor of `origin/main`. Card #28866 is closed.
- **"The key names are the maintainer's ruling of record `6580268872`, letter A" — right.** That comment on #28866 binds `client { clientId, clientSecret }` on the request and `client { source, clientId, hasSecret }` on the state, "the secret is never read back".
- **The connect door, closed body `{ clientId, clientSecret? }`, 400 refusals — right.** `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts#CONNECTOR_CONNECTION_BEGIN_BODY_KEYS` is `['clientId', 'clientSecret']`; `connectorConnectionBeginClientOf` answers an unknown key (and a `clientSecret` without `clientId`) as `400` with `code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`, and `respondToConnectorConnectionDoor` reads a body on `POST` only, handing it to the service as `client`. The service's `plugin.ts#installerClientOfBegin` refuses a `clientSource: 'installer'` instance begun without a client, and a client offered to an instance that declares its own or leaves it to MCP registration, both `credentialDoorRefusal(…, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', 400)`; it closes the key set again and judges the values. `refuseClientOffLeg` refuses a client on the read and revoke legs. The route is `POST /automation/connectors/:name/connection` in `route-ledger.ts`, served under the `/api/v1` base.
- **Authorize, exchange, refresh use the installer's client — right.** Begin: `buildAuthorizationUrl({ clientId: client?.clientId ?? installerClient?.clientId ?? auth.clientId })`, where on MCP discovery `client.clientId` is the installer's (passed as `declared.clientId`, `registered: false`). Complete: `requestOAuth2Token({ client: { clientId: client?.clientId ?? installerClient?.clientId …, clientSecret } })` with `clientSecret = installerClient?.clientSecret`. Refresh: `grant-handle.ts#endpointOf` reads the kept client through `parseKeptConnectionClient` and sends it.
- **Kept, encrypted through the `secret` channel, read back by `parseKeptConnectionClient` — right.** `sys-connector-connection.object.ts` declares `registered_client: Field.secret(…)`; `connect()` writes `serializeInstallerClient(installerClient, client)` into it; `resolveRegisteredClient` → `resolveSecret` → `installer-client.ts#parseKeptConnectionClient`. D3 on `main` already says "their secrets encrypted at rest through the `secret` channel (ADR-0100)".
- **A kept client of the wrong kind is a reconnect, never used — right.** `endpointOf`: `if (!kept || kept.installer !== (config.clientSource === 'installer')) return undefined`, and `refreshOnce` turns `undefined` into `grantRefused(current, reconnectRequiredReason(…, 'no_client'))`, which marks the row `reconnect_required` before refusing. The exchange leg has the matching check on the pending authorization (`takesInstallerClient(auth) !== (installerClient !== undefined)` → 400, code unused).
- **State `client { source: 'installer', clientId, hasSecret }`, never the secret — right.** `automation-service.ts#ConnectorConnectionState.client` is exactly that shape; `plugin.ts#describeConnection` fills it from the plain `client_id` / `client_has_secret` columns only.
- **No longer held degraded for a missing `clientId`; MCP over http discovers endpoints and registers no client — right.** `plugin.ts#oauth2NotServableReason` lists `clientId` as missing only when `auth.clientId === undefined && !takesInstallerClient(auth)`; `mcpDiscoveryServerUrl` counts the installer's client as supplied, and `mcpAuthorizationClient` passes it as `declared.clientId`, which `mcp-authorization.ts` takes "as is" (`registered: false`, no RFC 7591 call).
- **"The schema description no longer says the key is not served" — right.** `connector-auth.zod.ts#ConnectorInstanceOAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthSchema`'s `clientSource` description reads "The connection keeps the client encrypted, and every authorization, code exchange and refresh of that connection uses it (ADR-0143 D2.1)"; no "not served" / PLANNED wording, and `connector-auth-grant-kinds.test.ts` pins that.
- **"The ui slice is #28869, still open … the Console begins a connect with no client" — right.** #28869 is `open` with no linked PR; `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/setup/connectorConnections.ts#beginConnection` is `POST` with no body (its own doc line says so), so an installer instance gets `installerClientOfBegin`'s refusal, which names the vendor registration step and the redirect URI. PR #29097's body says the same.
- **The pins exist and hold the scenarios — right.** `connector-connection-door.test.ts` has the `describe("ADR-0143 D2.1 — an instance that takes the installer's OAuth client")` block (connect/refresh/revoke as the client, 400 without one, 400 on a malformed or misplaced client, read/revoke refuse a client, changed declaration uses no code, secret in no output); `connector-installer-oauth-client.dogfood.test.ts` pins "never for a missing `clientId`", the two 400s and the connected read naming the id, never the secret.

Nothing overstated. Two wording notes, neither a misstatement of behaviour (see ④).

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` label, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body: correct. `docs/adr/**` publishes nothing; no `packages/**` path in the diff. Check Changeset: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay of `os-steve`); no non-fleet login to name. `open_questions: []` in dev report `6581966146`. Two declared deviations, both answered: (a) no assignee / reviewer request was made through MCP — consistent with the standard order; a Tier H draft waits on a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval, which no reviewer request grants; (b) the PR footer is the repo's session-URL form — the repo's rule wins over the harness default. No `pm:prior-rulings` conflict: the note records rulings `6566728470` (B) and `6580268872` (A) and takes no decision of its own. The ADR index needs no regeneration (`check:adr-index` is part of the green `Lint · repo & tooling gates`).

### ④ Design judgment

`hits`: `docs/adr/0143-outbound-connector-auth-is-open-tier.md`. Judged against its first consumer (a reader of D2.1 deciding whether `clientSource: 'installer'` is served) and the execution plan it records (rulings B and A; server slice landed, ui slice open):

- **Holds.** Every sentence of the note is true of `origin/main` (① above). The note does what card #29256 asks and no more: the original sentence stays as the pre-#29097 state, dated and attributed; the note names the landing commit, the ruling of record for the key names, and the open ui slice with what the Console does until it lands. A reader can no longer take the key as declared-and-not-served.
- **Shape matches the repo's convention.** `**Amended (YYYY-MM-DD, #card) — title.**` as the first line of a blockquote, provenance in the first paragraph, then bullets — the same shape as the 2026-11-02 #28864 note above it, the 2026-10-31 #26710 note, and the list-nested notes in ADR-0005 (`  > **Amended (…`) and ADR-0087; a blockquote nested inside a bulleted blockquote (`>   > `) has precedent at ADR-0143 line 264 (note inside a D3 bullet) and the `> >` quotes in ADR-0048 / ADR-0087.
- **Anchors resolve.** The four symbol anchors name declarations the shared resolver's grammar accepts (`private installerClientOfBegin(`, `export function parseKeptConnectionClient(`, `const endpointOf = async`, `export interface ConnectorConnectionState`) and the two file anchors are tracked files on `origin/main`; `check:adr-symbol-anchors` runs in `Lint · docs & code guards`, green on this head.
- **should-fix (wording, no card owed on its own): "The grant handle uses it for authorize, exchange and refresh."** The claim that all three use the client is true, but in the tree `grant-handle.ts` is the refresh path only; the authorization URL and the code exchange are the plugin's begin/complete legs (`plugin.ts#beginConnectorConnection`, `#completeConnectorConnection`). The card used the same phrase, so the note repeats it; a later touch of this note could say "the connect and its grant handle".
- **should-fix (wording): "The rule is `plugin.ts#installerClientOfBegin`."** The key closure is enforced first at the runtime door (`automation.ts#connectorConnectionBeginClientOf`, which also refuses `clientSecret` without `clientId`), then again in the service; the service alone judges the values and the instance kind. The 400 outcome is as stated either way.

No must-fix.

Nothing red. The doc gates this diff answers to are complete and green: `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (`check:adr-anchors`, `check:adr-index`, `check:doc-authoring`), `Lint · docs & code guards` (`check:adr-symbol-anchors`), `Check Documentation Links`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`. The four pending runs touch no `docs/adr/**` input; the enqueue-time check still reads them all green before this PR moves (landing-operations clause ②).
